description: Black rot is a serious bacterial disease affecting cruciferous crops. It is caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas campestris pv. campestris and spreads mainly through infected seeds, plant debris, water splash, and contaminated tools. The pathogen enters plants through hydathodes at the leaf margins or through wounds, then spreads through the vascular system, causing characteristic blackened veins and leaf necrosis.
symptoms: Yellow V-shaped lesions starting from leaf margins
Lesions progressing toward the center of the leaf
Severe infections may cause plant death

monitoring: Regular field scouting for V-shaped lesions on leaves
Inspection of seedlings and young plants
Monitoring fields after periods of rain or high humidity
cultural_control: Practice crop rotation for at least 3–4 years
Remove and destroy infected plant residues
Avoid overhead irrigation to reduce leaf wetness
Plant resistant or tolerant varieties when available

chemical_control.note: Chemical control of bacterial diseases is limited. Copper-based bactericides are commonly used as preventive treatments.

economic_importance: Black rot can cause significant yield losses in cruciferous crops worldwide. Severe infections may destroy entire fields, particularly in warm and humid climates where the disease spreads rapidly.
